title: EcoFaaS: Rethinking the Design of Serverless Environments for Energy Efficiency
problem: Serverless functions execute in opaque virtualized sandboxes, are idle for a large fraction of their invocation time, context switch frequently, and are co-located dynamically with diverse functions, creating energy management challenges that existing schemes do not effectively address.
motivation: Serverless computing is increasingly popular but its energy and power consumption behavior is poorly understood, making energy-efficient design critical for cost and environmental sustainability.
method: EcoFaaS accepts a user-provided end-to-end application SLO and splits it into per-function deadlines that minimize total energy consumption. It predicts optimal per-invocation core frequency using fine-grained execution time analysis of each invocation accounting for specific inputs. The system partitions cores into multiple Core Pools where all cores in each pool run at the same frequency under a single scheduler, dynamically adjusting pool sizes and frequencies based on current system state.
key_novelty: First energy management framework specifically designed for serverless environments using per-function deadline splitting and dynamic core pool frequency management with invocation-aware execution prediction.
contributions: EcoFaaS: first energy management framework for serverless environments
Per-function deadline assignment algorithm minimizing total energy consumption while meeting application SLOs
Dynamic core pool management with fine-grained frequency scaling based on execution prediction
Implementation on OpenWhisk and KNative demonstrating 42% energy reduction and 34.8% tail latency improvement
limitations: Specific limitations and scope boundaries are not discussed in the abstract.
